playbook:
When I can already afford a settlement this turn, I post no offer.

When in the building phase I can afford a settlement I build the settlement (prefer 3 points now over delaying).

When I lack only one resource for a settlement, I post a single 1:1 offer to a player who has that resource and lacks what I'm offering.

When I lack wood but have surplus grain, I offer 1 grain for 1 wood to players who show wood in their holdings.

When I lack brick but have surplus ore (or vice versa), I offer 1 ore for 1 brick (or 1 brick for 1 ore) to the player who is the exclusive source of the needed resource.

When accepting posted offers, I accept any combination that lets me complete the highest-value build available this round (settlement > road). If an offer only enables a road and costs a scarce resource that I need for a settlement, I decline.

When multiple offers are posted to me, I choose the one that yields the build with the largest immediate point gain; if equal, choose the trade that preserves scarce resources for future settlement builds.

Do not post trades that would give opponents a resource they need to immediately build a settlement, unless the trade is necessary for me to build a settlement that same round.

Do not accept trades that hand away a unique scarce resource (e.g., my last brick) for a low-value return unless doing so enables a strictly higher immediate point outcome.

When I cannot build this round and no single 1:1 trade gets me a settlement next round, prefer to conserve flexible resources (grain/ore) and only offer exact 1:1 swaps that improve my chances of building next turn.

Avoid multi-resource or multi-party offers—use simple 1:1 offers naming a specific counterparty and resource to keep trades predictable and to avoid empowering opponents unnecessarily.

1.text:
When I'm in the build phase and I can afford a settlement, I build the settlement (prefer 3 points now over a road's 1).

When I'm in the build phase and I cannot afford a settlement but can afford a road, I build the road only if the road is the best immediate-scoring option and I have no clear path to a settlement next turn.

When I'm allowed to post a trade, I post at most one 1-for-1 offer and name a specific counterparty who visibly has a surplus of the resource I need.

When I post a trade, I only offer a resource I can spare without preventing me from building this round (unless I have a clear plan and buffer).

When an offer is posted to me, I accept it if and only if accepting enables an immediate build that increases my score, or it guarantees a higher-scoring build on the next turn without handing the opponent the win.

When an offer would leave me without a resource that is uniquely required to build this turn (e.g., the only brick or the only wood I have), I decline it.

When choosing trading partners, I prefer to deal with players who recently showed willingness to trade that resource (past trades) or who have stockpiles of it.

When I cannot build this turn and no good trade is available, I post no offer rather than making a risky or lopsided trade.

Do not accept trades that mainly benefit the opponent's ability to score immediately unless I get equal immediate benefit.

Do not make multi-resource or uneven offers unless I have a strategic reason and buffer; stick to simple 1-for-1s to keep options flexible.

2.text:
When my holdings include at least 1 wood, 1 brick, 1 grain, and 1 ore, I build a settlement immediately.

When I can only afford a road (1 wood + 1 brick) but could reach a settlement next round with one more resource, prefer saving resources for the settlement unless the extra point from the road will change the end-game outcome.

When I lack any resource needed to build this round, post one trade offer to get the single most blocking resource (the one that completes a settlement first, then a road). Name a counterparty who has that resource.

When posting an offer, give a resource I have in surplus (2+ of) or one that is least useful for current goals; ask only for the exact resource I need. Do not overtrade.

When an offer is posted to me, accept it if the incoming resource completes a build I can perform this round (settlement preferred over road), or if it advances me to a clear next-turn build priority; otherwise decline.

When multiple identical offers come in that each cost me the same resource (e.g., both want 1 wood for 1 grain), accept only as many as are necessary for my immediate build or plan — avoid turning all of one scarce resource into duplicates of another unless that other is what I need.

When I have 0 of a resource that blocks every feasible build (e.g., no brick), prioritize trading for that resource over hoarding potential city materials (grain/ore) unless a city is immediately reachable and more valuable.

When I can build nothing and a trade would convert a resource I need into one I don't (e.g., giving wood when I actually need brick), refuse or counteroffer for the specific resource I need.

When choosing between trading with opponents, prefer the counterparty who has less use for what I offer (more likely to accept) and who is not racing to the same immediate build unless the trade benefits me more than them.

When offered a straightforward 1:1 swap that gets me from “cannot build” to “can build a settlement,” accept immediately.

When I can complete a city (if that mechanic exists) in one trade and it yields more points than a settlement, prioritize that trade; but do not sacrifice the single blocking resource for a later goal if it prevents me from scoring now and the opponent can immediately use it to score.

What did not work: do not keep a single grain (or other city material) instead of trading it when doing so leaves me unable to obtain the single resource (brick) that would let me build a settlement and score now.
